back2basics.text: An Export Promotion Mission is a government initiative designed to enhance a country's export competitiveness by providing financial and non-financial support to exporters. It typically includes interventions to improve market access, compliance with international standards, and logistics infrastructure, especially targeting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Such missions help exporters overcome barriers to international trade and expand into new markets.

2026-11-19-am-0a388397d0.deck: On 17 November 2026, the Department of Commerce amended guidelines under four interventions of the Export Promotion Mission to enhance support for MSME exporters. These changes aim to improve market access, compliance assistance, and logistics support, especially for exporters in low export-intensity areas.

body: Describe the amendments in Market Access Support, including increased airfare reimbursement and turnover limits.

structure.intro: The Export Promotion Mission aims to enhance India's export competitiveness, particularly for MSMEs, through targeted interventions.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the recent amendments under the Export Promotion Mission:
1. The maximum eligible export turnover for airfare reimbursement under Market Access Support was increased from ₹75 lakh to ₹50 crore.
2. The Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT) now includes waterways as a mode of transport and extends air freight support to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: A common trap is to confuse the previous turnover limit (₹75 lakh) with the new limit (₹50 crore) or to overlook the extension of air freight support to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh under LIFT.

body.label: Market Access Support (MAS)
body.text: The maximum eligible export turnover for airfare reimbursement increased from ₹75 lakh to ₹50 crore, with airfare reimbursement raised to 95% for micro and small exporters and 80% for others; the mandatory Export Promotion Council membership period was reduced from six to three months.

body.label: Trade Regulations, Accreditation & Compliance Enablement (TRACE)
body.text: The list of certificates eligible for reimbursement expanded from 462 to 600, helping MSMEs meet international quality, safety, and technical standards.

body.label: Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT)
body.text: Coverage of low export-intensity districts expanded from 13 to 34 States/UTs; eligible ports now include Land Customs Stations and Integrated Check Posts; waterways added as a transport mode; air freight support extended to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh; minimum distance criterion reduced from 200 km to 100 km; support extended to all exportable merchandise except those in a negative list.

sections.heading: What changes were made under the Export Promotion Mission?

body.label: Enhanced financial support
body.text: Higher airfare reimbursements and increased turnover limits reduce cost barriers for MSMEs to participate in international trade events.

body.label: Improved compliance assistance
body.text: Expanding eligible certificates helps MSMEs meet global standards, facilitating smoother market entry and competitiveness.

body.label: Addressing logistical challenges
body.text: Expanding geographic coverage and transport modes lowers freight costs and improves export feasibility for MSMEs in remote or low export-intensity areas.

sections.heading: Why do these changes matter for MSME exporters?

body.label: Mission approval and funding
body.text: The Union Cabinet approved the Export Promotion Mission on 12 November 2025 with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31.

body.label: Mission objectives
body.text: It aims to strengthen India's export competitiveness via financial and non-financial support, focusing on MSMEs, first-time exporters, and under-represented regions.

body.label: Sub-schemes and interventions
body.text: The Mission operates through two sub-schemes: Niryat Protsahan (trade finance access) and Niryat Disha (market access and non-financial barriers), with 11 interventions operational so far.

back2basics.text: The electoral roll is an official list of eligible voters maintained by the Election Commission. Voter enumeration is the process of registering voters and updating the roll to reflect changes such as deaths, shifts, or duplicates. Forms like Form 6 are used for new voter registration, while Form 7 is used for corrections or deletions. Accurate rolls ensure fair elections by preventing fraud and disenfranchisement.

2026-11-19-am-2aca9fe25d.deck: A public interest litigation in the Supreme Court seeks disclosure of how many voters removed under absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories have refilled enumeration forms to re-enter electoral rolls. This issue highlights concerns about electoral roll accuracy and voter rights, relevant for electoral reforms and democratic processes.

body: Challenges include removal of voters under ASDD categories and procedural errors in form usage.
Judicial scrutiny, such as the recent Supreme Court PIL, ensures transparency and protects voters from wrongful disenfranchisement.
Election Commission directives and audits are necessary to correct errors and prevent misuse by political agents.
Transparency in the process strengthens electoral integrity and public trust.
structure.conclusion: Judicial oversight complements administrative efforts to maintain accurate electoral rolls and uphold democratic rights.
structure.intro: Accurate electoral rolls are fundamental to democratic elections and voter rights.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about voter enumeration and electoral roll updates in the context of the recent Supreme Court PIL:
1. Form 6 is intended for new voter registration but was misused by voters removed under ASDD categories to re-enter rolls.
2. The Election Commission allowed voters removed under ASDD categories in seven states to submit enumeration forms instead of Form 6.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: A trap is confusing the role of Form 7 with Form 6; Form 7 relates to corrections or deletions, not new registrations.

body.label: ASDD voter removal
body.text: Voters marked as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate (ASDD) were deleted from draft electoral rolls during a Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

body.label: Submission of enumeration forms
body.text: Some ASDD voters submitted enumeration forms to be restored to the rolls, but the exact number is unknown and sought by petitioners.

body.label: Form 6 misuse
body.text: Form 6, meant for new voter registration, was used by excluded voters to re-enter rolls, which the Supreme Court called an 'error' since it requires applicants to declare they are first-time voters.

body.label: Election Commission directive
body.text: The Election Commission allowed ASDD voters in seven states, including Delhi, to submit enumeration forms again instead of using Form 6.

body.label: Concerns over Form 7 misuse
body.text: The petition also raised concerns about misuse of Form 7 for targeted deletions and requested an audit and public disclosure of all Form 7 applications.

body.label: Transparency in political party role
body.text: It was requested that booth-level agents filing Form 7 identify themselves as party representatives rather than individuals.

sections.heading: What is the issue with voter enumeration and electoral rolls?

body.label: Voter rights protection
body.text: Ensuring voters removed under ASDD categories can restore their names protects their right to vote and prevents disenfranchisement.

body.label: Electoral roll accuracy
body.text: Accurate and updated electoral rolls are essential for free and fair elections, preventing fraud and errors.

body.label: Transparency and accountability
body.text: Public disclosure of enumeration and deletion data, and transparency about political party involvement, strengthen electoral integrity.

body.label: Legal clarity on forms
body.text: Clarifying correct use of forms like Form 6 and Form 7 prevents procedural errors and misuse in voter registration and deletion.

back2basics.concept: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)
back2basics.text: CBDR-RC is a principle under international environmental law recognizing that while all countries are responsible for addressing global environmental destruction, they have different capabilities and differing responsibilities based on their historical contributions to the problem. It underpins climate negotiations by emphasizing equity and fairness in climate action commitments.

2026-11-19-am-86c55a5ef0.deck: At COP31 in Antalya, India highlighted its climate diplomacy focusing on equity, climate justice, and sustainable development while advancing mechanisms like the India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism and promoting disaster-resilient infrastructure. These developments are crucial for UPSC aspirants to understand India’s international climate stance and its domestic and global climate action strategies.

body.label: India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism
body.text: India operationalized the India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, signed in August 2025, to mobilise finance, facilitate technology transfer, and advance low-carbon development aligned with India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS).

body.label: Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure
body.text: India positioned the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) as a global platform to strengthen infrastructure resilience through international cooperation, emphasizing knowledge sharing, capacity building, and affordable sustainable finance.

sections.heading: What key climate initiatives did India highlight at COP31?

body.label: Equity and Climate Justice
body.text: India called for climate action rooted in equity, climate justice, and the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), stressing that developing countries should not bear the burden of historical emissions.

body.label: Climate Finance Obligations
body.text: India urged developed countries to honestly and expeditiously fulfil their climate finance obligations and cautioned against unilateral trade measures penalizing developing countries under the guise of climate action.

body.label: Development and Climate Action
body.text: India emphasized that developing countries must not choose between climate action and their right to development, decent living standards, health, and education, and insisted on equitable access to the remaining carbon budget.

sections.heading: What principles and demands did India emphasize in its climate diplomacy?

body.label: Indus Waters Treaty Context
body.text: India stated that sharing of transboundary river waters cannot be based on 'archaic mechanisms' or divorced from the broader bilateral relationship, indirectly referring to the Indus Waters Treaty being in abeyance since 2025 due to cross-border terrorism concerns.

body.label: Need for Contemporary Cooperation
body.text: India highlighted the importance of considering climatic, demographic, and technological changes in transboundary water cooperation and reiterated that constructive cooperation can lead to shared progress and prosperity.

back2basics.concept: Counter-terrorism operations in Jammu and Kashmir
back2basics.text: Counter-terrorism operations in Jammu and Kashmir involve coordinated efforts by multiple security agencies including the police, army, paramilitary forces, and intelligence agencies. These operations aim to neutralise terrorists, prevent attacks, and dismantle terror networks while balancing security with civilian safety. The 'Whole of Government approach' ensures synergy among all stakeholders to effectively address terrorism and related threats.

2026-11-19-am-935225df2e.deck: Lashkar-e-Taiba's last known active local terrorist in Kashmir, Lateef Bhat, was neutralised in a joint operation by J&K Police, Army, CRPF, and intelligence agencies in Kulgam in November 2026. This marks a significant development in India's counter-terrorism efforts in Jammu and Kashmir, relevant for understanding internal security dynamics and government strategies against terrorism.

Consider the following statements about the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba's last known local terrorist in Kashmir:

body.label: Identity and background
body.text: Lateef Ahmad Bhat was the last known active local Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist in Kashmir, involved in multiple attacks including the November 11, 2026 attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam.

body.label: Encounter details
body.text: In a joint operation by J&K Police, Indian Army, CRPF, and intelligence agencies, Bhat was killed in a gunfight in Kulgam on November 18, 2026, after refusing to surrender despite a video call urging him to do so.

body.label: Associated terrorist neutralised
body.text: One of Bhat's associates, Umar Nisar Dar, was neutralised in Kulgam a day before the encounter with Bhat.

sections.heading: Who was Lateef Bhat and what happened in the encounter?

body.label: End of local active terrorists
body.text: With Bhat's killing, for the first time since militancy began in 1989, there is no listed active local terrorist in Kashmir Valley, marking a milestone in counter-terrorism.

body.label: Ongoing threat from foreign operatives
body.text: Despite the elimination of local terrorists, around 30 Pakistani operatives remain active in Kashmir, indicating continued cross-border terrorism threats.

body.label: Government's coordinated approach
body.text: The operation demonstrated high synergy among security forces, reflecting the 'Whole of Government approach' emphasised in national counter-terrorism policy.

sections.heading: Why does this matter for India's internal security?

body.label: Civilian hardships
body.text: Prolonged security operations in civilian areas of Kulgam led to restrictions affecting local populations, drawing criticism from political parties about collective punishment and hardships.

body.label: Sanctity of religious places
body.text: Security forces displayed restraint to preserve the sanctity of the mosque where Bhat was hiding during the encounter.

sections.heading: What challenges and concerns arose during the operation?
